title.narrative: Integrated response to needs in Education, Child protection and, WASH for underserved communities, including the most vulnerable school-aged girls and boys, in Aleppo, Dar'a, and Rural Damascus

description.narrative: ltpgtAligned with the 2024 HRPs, this project directly contributes to the 2 objectives of SHF’s 1st allocation strategy by delivering critical basic services and enhancing resilience in underserved areas. The project focuses on localities with demonstrated high needs low response coverage through an integrated approach with education, CP, and WaSH activities.lt/pgtltpgtThe response is informed by TGH's 6 years of experience implementing multi sectoral projects funded by ECHO, SHF, and SDC in Syria. The targeted locations are prioritised sub-districts for this allocation, all having inter-sector severity of 4. Field assessments from May-July 24 involved coordination with municipalities, SARC, DoE/DoW, and other NGOs. TGH's integrated intervention will take place in Busra Esh-Sham (Dar’a), Hosh Elfara (RD), As-Safira (Aleppo), and Jaberiyeh / Um Krouh (Aleppo). Additionally, WaSH activities will be carried out in Duma, part of Duma sub-district in Rural Damascus governorate, which includes Hosh Elfara. As part of the CE and based on assessment, Arbin has been identified as a high-need area and added for an integrated intervention. Selected in coordination with sectors and authorities, Arbin is expected to receive a high number of returnees and has sustained significant damage to infrastructure. Following clashes in Sweida and subsequent displacements in Dar’a, TGH will mobilize WASH emergency capacity to support HHs displaced in Busra.ltbrgtThe main objective is to enhance the resilience of underserved communities, especially vulnerable school-aged girls and boys, by improving access to safe, inclusive, and protected education services and essential life-saving WASH services. The project will reach 126,436 individuals, including community members from WaSH rehabilitations (up from 114,800 previous to CE) in addition, of 556 individuals from the Sweida response, 3,572 through Education (previously 1,960), and 1,656 through CP (previously 1,291). The increase is due to the addition of the As-Safira network rehabilitation Arbin locality and Sweida response (August 2025).ltbrgtWASH:ltbrgtRehabilitation of water sanitation systems and schools, including WASH facilitiesltbrgtSustain access to basic WASH services by installing solar panels and building capacity of WAltbrgtPromotion of correct usage of rehabilitated WASH facilities through HP and soap provisionltbrgtDistribution of hygiene kits and cleaning kits (August 2025)ltbrgtEducation:ltbrgtImprove access to quality education by addressing the needs of OOSC and children at risk of dropping outltbrgtIdentify OOSC and favour their return to education through BTL campaignsltbrgtBuild teacher capacities and provide NFE activities ltbrgtMitigate financial barriers to education by providing kits transportation support for teachers from remote areasltbrgtStrengthen community resilience engagement through CBECPCltbrgtInitiation of PTM to foster the relationship between parents/caregivers and schoolsltbrgtCP:ltbrgtOffer PSS, including risk education and recreational activities, to studentsltbrgtTrain teachers on PSS topics and awareness campaigns for parentsltbrgtSupport children with disabilities, early married girls, and child labor cases, offering case management and referrals as part of CP mainstreamingltbrgtComplemented by other interventions from TGH and partners in surrounding locations, with coordination from local and international partners ensuring a cohesive approach and avoiding duplication.ltbrgtCE: Numbers updated in the text. The extension includes Arbin and As-Safira, high-priority WASH areas, improving water access and supporting returnees. In education and CP, Arbin school will receive urgent repairs and furniture to enhance learning conditions. Additionally, education and CP activities will be extended to Aug-25, ensuring continuity, bridging learning gaps for returnees, and reducing dropout risks. By integrating WaSH, education, and CP, the project strengthens resilience, fosters social cohesion, and allows TGH to better meet its objectives while adapting to the evolving contextltbrgtlt/pgt
